--- name: decard description: Find and remove card-based UI container components — shadcn/MUI/Bootstrap/Vuetify/Ant/Chakra Card, elevated "box" panels, bordered-and-shadowed wrappers — and flatten them into section + heading + divider layouts. Also prevents reaching for card containers when building new UI. Use when the user says "remove cards", "no cards", "no card containers", "flatten cards", "decard", "de-card", "find cards", "de-overlay", "too boxy", or wants a flatter / less-boxed design. Keeps structural borders on tables, lists, and code blocks. --- # decard — flatten card-based containers A card container is a **box that wraps a section of content** purely to elevate it: rounded corners + border + (usually) a shadow, with a header/title slot and a body slot. It adds a visual frame the content does not need. `decard` removes that frame and lets content sit flat on the page, separated by headings and thin rules instead of stacked boxes. Two modes, both driven by this one rule set: - **Remove** — find existing card containers and flatten them. - **Prevent** — when building or reviewing UI, do not introduce card containers in the first place. ## What counts as a card container (remove these) - Component libraries: `` / `` / `` / `` (shadcn/ui), `` / `` (MUI), `` (Vuetify), `` (Element), `` (Ant), `` (Chakra/Mantine), `` (Angular Material), Bootstrap `class="card"`. - Hand-rolled equivalents: a wrapper `
` whose only job is `rounded-* border … shadow…` (or `bg-card` / `bg-white` + `shadow`) around a titled block of content. ## What to KEEP (do NOT strip these) Flattening ≠ removing every border. Keep structural borders where content would otherwise run together or look broken: - **Tables** — keep their `border` + `rounded` frame. - **Lists of rows** — keep one outer `border` + `divide-y` (a single divided list reads better than N boxes; collapse a grid of identical cards into this). - **Code blocks / pre** — keep their frame. - **Inputs / textareas** — keep their border. - **A single stat strip** — one bordered grid is fine; a wall of stat boxes is not. The test: does the border separate genuinely different data, or does it just gift-wrap a paragraph + heading? Wrap → cut it. Separate data → keep it. ## Flatten recipe Replace: ``` Title Subtitle …content… ``` with: ```

Title

Subtitle

…content…
``` - Separate sections with generous spacing (`space-y-8` / `space-y-10`) and/or a single hairline `` between major groups — not a box each. - A **grid of identical cards** → one bordered `
    ` with `divide-y` rows. - The card's title becomes a plain heading that sits **above** the content, not inside a frame. - Drop elevation: remove `shadow-*` on any panel that survives. If the project has a shared `Card` primitive, deleting its `shadow` de-boxes everything at once. - After flattening, remove now-unused `Card*` imports. ## How to find them Search the codebase / current diff (adapt globs to the stack): ``` rg -n "]|Card(Header|Content|Title|Description|Footer)|` + heading + spacing first. Only add a border when it frames a table, a divided list, a code block, or an input. - Never wrap a heading + paragraph + buttons in a bordered/shadowed box "for structure" — spacing and a heading already give structure. - No nested cards, ever (a card inside a card is two frames too many). ## Boundary This skill governs container chrome, not information. Do not delete content, data, controls, or accessibility affordances — only the box around them. If a "card" is actually a meaningful interactive unit (a selectable tile, a draggable item, a clickable result with its own hover state), keep it; flatten the decorative panels, not the functional ones.

# decard

A cross-agent **skill + slash command** that finds and removes card-based UI
container components — shadcn/MUI/Bootstrap/Vuetify/Ant/Chakra `Card`, elevated
"box" panels, bordered-and-shadowed wrappers — and flattens them into
`section` + heading + divider layouts. It also prevents reaching for card
containers when building new UI.

Flattening is **not** "remove every border": tables, divided lists, code blocks
and inputs keep their structural frames. Only the decorative box that gift-wraps
a heading + prose gets cut, and a grid of identical cards collapses into one
divided list.

## Repo layout

```
skills/decard/SKILL.md      # the skill (Agent Skills standard)
skills.sh.json              # skills.sh repo grouping
.claude/commands/decard.md  # Claude Code  ->  /decard
.opencode/commands/decard.md# OpenCode     ->  /decard
.pi/prompts/decard.md       # pi           ->  /decard   (also /skill:decard)
```

The full rule set, flatten recipe and search patterns live in
[`skills/decard/SKILL.md`](./skills/decard/SKILL.md).

## Install

### skills.sh

This repo follows the [skills.sh](https://www.skills.sh) layout
(`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` + `skills.sh.json`). Point the skills.sh tooling /
registry at `github.com/Akicou/decard`; the `decard` skill appears under the
**UI cleanup** group.

### Claude Code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Akicou/decard.git /tmp/decard
# Skill (auto-loads on relevant requests):
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -r /tmp/decard/skills/decard ~/.claude/skills/decard
# Slash command  ->  /decard
mkdir -p ~/.claude/commands
cp /tmp/decard/.claude/commands/decard.md ~/.claude/commands/decard.md
```

> `cp` won't create the target folder — the `mkdir -p` lines matter. On PowerShell
> use `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force <dir>` (mkdir's `-p` is implied by `-Force`).

### pi (pi.dev)

```bash
# Skill  ->  /skill:decard
mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/skills
cp -r /tmp/decard/skills/decard ~/.pi/agent/skills/decard
# Prompt template  ->  /decard
mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/prompts
cp /tmp/decard/.pi/prompts/decard.md ~/.pi/agent/prompts/decard.md
```

### OpenCode

```bash
# Command  ->  /decard   (global; or use ./.opencode/commands/ per-project)
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/commands
cp /tmp/decard/.opencode/commands/decard.md ~/.config/opencode/commands/decard.md
```

### Other agents (Cursor, Cline, …)

Any agent that runs a markdown prompt can use the same body — copy the contents
of [`.claude/commands/decard.md`](./.claude/commands/decard.md) into that tool's
command/rule format.

## Use

Trigger it in any project:

- `/decard` — flatten cards in the current diff (or the whole UI)
- `/decard src/pages/Settings.tsx` — target a path
- `/decard audit` — just list the card containers, don't edit
- or plain language: "remove the cards", "this is too boxy", "de-overlay the UI"

---
description: Find and flatten card-based UI containers into section + divider layouts
argument-hint: "[path | \"audit\"]  (default: current diff, else the whole UI)"
---

Apply the **decard** method to: $ARGUMENTS

A *card container* is a box that exists only to wrap a titled chunk of content and
elevate it — shadcn/MUI/Bootstrap/Vuetify/Ant/Chakra `Card`, or a hand-rolled
`rounded-* + border + shadow` `<div>` around a heading + prose. Find them and flatten:

- Replace `<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle/></CardHeader><CardContent>…</CardContent></Card>`
  with `<section>` + a plain heading + the content. Separate sections with spacing
  (`space-y-8`) or a single hairline divider — not a box each.
- Collapse a **grid of identical cards** into one bordered `<ul>` with `divide-y` rows.
- Drop `shadow-*` on any panel that survives. If a shared `Card` primitive ends up
  unused, point it out (don't silently delete a library primitive).
- Remove now-unused `Card*` imports, then build / type-check.

KEEP structural borders on **tables, divided lists, code blocks, and inputs** — flattening
is not "remove every border", only the decorative box around a heading + prose. Don't touch
functional/interactive tiles (selectable, draggable, clickable-with-hover). Report each
change as `path:line`.

If `$ARGUMENTS` is empty, work on the current diff; if there is none, scan the UI source.
If it is `audit`, only list the card containers you find — do not edit.
